R404.note: Control characters, DEL, backslash and Unicode line separators are escaped before the winston sink; the switch from simple() to json() format and the move of the username into a metadata field are stated in the write-up and block no caller (the JSON formatter double-escapes the encoded backslashes, which is cosmetic).

R405.note: Exact-match allowlist of fixed ORDER BY strings before orderByRaw is the right shape for an identifier sink and the contract calls for approved modes only; the InvalidArgumentException on other values is stated, though the write-up assumes created_at asc/desc are the only approved modes.

R406.note: Registering /settings/email on protectedMux puts it behind the CSRF middleware; handler, 405 path and profile route unchanged.

R407.note: createCipheriv with AES-256-GCM, a random 12-byte IV and a PBKDF2-derived key replaces the deprecated createCipher; the added salt/iv/authTag response fields are stated and the ciphertext field remains.

R408.note: crypto/rand via io.ReadFull with 128 bits hex-encoded replaces math/rand; the token changing from decimal digits to 32 hex characters is stated and the Go 1.24 error-handling claim is accurate.

R409.note: Swapping text/template for html/template gives contextual escaping of {{.Subject}} with no other change.

R410.note: %15s closes the stack overflow correctly, but a token longer than 15 characters is now silently truncated (returns 0 with a partial code and leaves the remainder in stdin) rather than rejected with -1 as the contract requires, and the write-up does not mention this.

R411.note: Rejecting non-null getHost() blocks //evil and absolute URLs, but an opaque value with a scheme and no authority such as https:evil.example passes both checks and Tomcat sends it verbatim as Location (browser resolves it to the external host when the scheme differs from the page's); the fix also rejects absolute same-host URLs the original accepted (stated), and the write-up calls the closed failure mode 'fails open'.

R412.note: IsAuthenticated closes anonymous access but any logged-in user can still list, create and destroy every owner's internal API keys including the secret key field, so authorization is still missing; the restriction added is what the finding calls for.

R413.note: Clamping length with std::min stops the out-of-bounds read, but an over-long window now returns a checksum of a silently truncated range instead of being rejected, which the contract forbids unless reported to callers; the write-up states the clamp but the caller cannot tell.

R414.note: Role check for admin after authentication and before SuspendUser, returning 403; nothing else changes.

R415.note: Standard it = erase(it) / ++it idiom removes every completed task, preserves order and evaluates every element.

R416.note: Capturing a shared_ptr keeps the Widget alive until the queued callback runs; the startTimer signature change and make_shared in handleRequest are stated, though passing self separately from this allows a mismatched pointer.

R417.note: Offset and underflow-safe length checks before subspan close the read; the empty-vector return for an invalid header is stated (callers cannot distinguish it from a legitimate zero-length field, a minor ambiguity).

R418.note: Wrapping exportUsersHandler in the existing requireAdmin matches the sibling routes and changes nothing else.

R419.note: With a .bat target cmd.exe re-parses the argument so an allowlist is the only workable shape and ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ excludes every batch metacharacter; it is nonetheless a new restriction that rejects report names the original accepted (spaces, other characters) via IllegalArgumentException, stated in the write-up.
